units.unit: Topic is Hong Kong's subdivided flats and the housing policy debate around them
Wants a broad descriptive overview of who lives in subdivided units and why
It is for an essay setting up who ends up in subdivided units and why they are there
Has no claim yet; wants a descriptive source to anchor the opening
Wants a descriptive overview plus a first-hand tenant account to anchor the opening
Wants a large-scale survey of SDU tenants with numbers on what they would trade for security or a faster housing offer
Wants a document laying out the supply picture and elasticity estimates
Tenant-side piece should quantify with percentages what households would accept for security or a faster offer
Supply side should give elasticity estimates, ideally a range, showing responsiveness of stock to rent
Wants to test whether the interviewed tenant's waiting-list framing is idiosyncratic or representative
Needs survey trade-offs, supply elasticity, and stock data for tenant-side and supply-side claims
Needs a tenant trade-off survey and a supply elasticity paper
Needs a Berlin case study for comparative evidence
Still needs Hong Kong enforcement and legal material: inspection capacity and legal opinion on instruments
Inspection-capacity piece supports a practical objection that a tightened cap could not be enforced across the stock
Legal opinion is meant to show what instrument a careful lawyer thinks is defensible instead
For inspection capacity needs evidence of how much of the stock inspectors actually reach
For the legal opinion needs a definition of the instruments and their legal footing
Needs enforcement capacity and legal instrument footing
Wants one last source on the landlord side and actual margin economics
Keeps hearing that owners can't absorb anything
Wants a landlord's own account in plain terms of what they can and can't absorb
Wants to test the claim that owners can't take any cut against a real voice rather than a slogan
